clue.text: Try a box of wine, it's an example to follow

parts.note: to try something is to test it
wine is sold by the case, a box of a dozen bottles

explanation.surface: Someone sampling a crate of wine and declaring it a model for others.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome sets a precedent that later cases follow.

clue.text: Flog rubbish with leader of Harrods involved

indicators.note: involved means wrapped up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: rubbish means trash

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone trying to sell junk with the boss of a famous London store in on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrods is a grand London department store; only its first letter is used, placed inside TRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog someone is to beat or whip them, which is what thrash also means.

clue.text: Food at the pig's ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of the words before it are reworked

parts.note: these words supply their own letters, the S of pig's included

explanation.surface: A farmyard picture of something to eat found on the ground where the pig lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like the noun for the pig's patch, but it is the past tense of grind, signalling the anagram of ATTHEPIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a kind of pasta, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Something to put a smile on your face, no problem

definitions.text: Something to put a smile on your face, no problem

parts.words: Something to put a smile on your face, no problem
parts.note: read the phrase literally: a surgeon reshapes the face, and the procedure is cosmetic rather than treating any medical problem

explanation.surface: A cheery advert for something that makes you happy with no trouble at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic surgery done for looks alone can literally fix a smile onto someone's face without any illness to treat.

clue.text: Place to play spades with stone

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
with means and, joining two things
a stone in a fruit is its pit

explanation.surface: A child's play area involving spades and a stone, the tools of digging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' looks like digging tools beside the sandpit, but it is the card suit abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandpit is a box of sand where children play.

clue.text: Stiffness shown by lead actor going to Switzerland

parts.note: the lead actor in a show is its star
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: A leading actor seems rather stiff after moving to Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is the substance used to stiffen fabric, and by extension stiffness of manner.

clue.text: Retire by the second

parts.note: in boxing a fighter is retired from a bout when his second, the corner man, tosses a cloth into the ring

explanation.surface: Someone quitting in a hurry, as if within a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' suggests a moment of time, but it is the boxer's assistant in the corner.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede defeat comes from the boxing second signalling surrender by tossing his cloth into the ring.

clue.text: European river runs just short of street

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letters for street are taken away

parts.note: just means fair or honest

explanation.surface: A river in Europe flows just shy of reaching the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only', but it is the adjective meaning fair, HONEST, which loses ST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone flows through Switzerland and France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Gardener's tool used by firemen

parts.note: a single piece of equipment that waters a garden and also, much bigger, carries water to a fire

explanation.surface: A piece of garden kit that fire crews also rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible tube for carrying water serves both the gardener and the fire brigade.

clue.text: Vegetables rising from south-eastern early morning dampness-es

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: dew is early morning dampness, and the coined plural gives dews

explanation.surface: Root crops coming up out of damp south-eastern ground at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the whole of SE plus DEWS, giving SWEDES; the setter's 'dampness-es' is a jokey plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are large root vegetables, also called rutabagas.

clue.text: Raises lugs on the end of lawnmower

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece
the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: lugs is informal British for ears

explanation.surface: The handles fixed on the back of a lawnmower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lugs' looks like handles on the mower, but it is slang for ears.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear something is to lift or raise it, as a horse rears up.

clue.text: Possibly Morse owns places for collating info

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse might own the rooms where intelligence is gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse here looks like the TV detective or the code, but it is only anagram fodder with OWNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsrooms are offices where reporters gather and assemble information into news.

clue.text: Dragged and rushed around nasty lech, adding pressure

indicators.note: around means one piece goes about the other

parts.note: sped is another word for rushed, the past tense of speed

indicators.note: nasty signals the letters of lech are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone pulled along and hurried away from an unpleasant lecher under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' looks like a description of the lecher, but it is the anagram signal; 'adding' just tacks the pressure letter on before the lot goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep is to haul or drag something laboriously, a word from Yiddish.

clue.text: Bear with nanny, say

parts.note: a nanny is an example of hired domestic help

explanation.surface: A teddy bear sitting with the nanny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a noun, but it is the verb to give birth; whelp is to give birth to puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth to young, as a bitch does, so it is to bear offspring.

clue.text: Spartan area I had turned and left

indicators.note: left means gone away, so these letters depart from the word

parts.note: a district is an area

indicators.note: turned means the letters are put in reverse order

parts.note: I had is shortened to I'd

explanation.surface: An area that a Spartan had turned away from and quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ID to DI, and 'left' removes DI from DISTRICT.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and severe, like the strict discipline of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: Ridicules sentences in US

definitions.meaning: to ridicule is to mock or parody
in American slang to send someone up is to sentence them to prison, as in 'sent up the river'

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is American: being sent up is going to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To parody someone is to mock them, and in America to send a criminal to jail.

clue.text: A source of food? Something to get you going in emergency!

definitions.meaning: humorously, a roll of fat round the waist from overeating

definitions.text: Something to get you going in emergency!
definitions.meaning: an extra wheel kept in a car for a puncture

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a joke: the belly bulge comes from food.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an extra wheel carried in a car and a roll of belly fat.

clue.text: School dance when wife is married-a sentimental production

indicators.note: when one thing is another means the first letter is swapped for the second
when one thing is another means the first letter is swapped for the second

parts.note: a waltz is a dance

explanation.surface: A school dance where the bride is married off, a soppy affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of WALTZ is replaced by M.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is excessive sentimentality in art or music.

clue.text: Embarrassed lad on unfinished break-in, say

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece
unfinished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a break-in is an example of a crime
a lad is a son

explanation.surface: A boy blushing after being caught in a half-done burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed goes red in the face, so crimson describes that blushing state.

clue.text: Close to bare bum in New York

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other piece
bum as an adjective means bad or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone close to baring their bottom in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like a bottom, but it is the American adjective for bad, anagramming BARE to EARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close to or not far from.

clue.text: Concerning hot lunch, perhaps warm up

parts.note: RE means concerning, as in a letter heading
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
having lunch is an example of eating

explanation.surface: Worried about a hot lunch, someone thinks to warm it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat food is to warm it up again.

clue.text: Rush around not careful but calm

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes about the second

parts.note: a rush is a reed, a waterside plant
lax means slack or not careful

explanation.surface: Someone who rushes about carelessly yet stays calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb meaning hurry, but it is the plant, REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed means at ease, untroubled and calm.

clue.text: Tough con takes in rookie at first

indicators.note: takes in means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: to con is to study, as to con a book

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A hardened conman lets a newcomer in at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' looks like a swindler or prisoner, but it is the old verb meaning to study.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means robust and strong, so tough.

clue.text: Scrooge's man ignoring tradition at first

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Ebenezer Scrooge, a man who ignores the traditions of Christmas at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrooge, the skinflint in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, has become a byword for a mean person.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrooge is a mean, money-hoarding person, after Dickens's character.

clue.text: Don't go to bed early, drink includes old vermouth

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sup is to drink
IT is old slang for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Advice not to retire early but to have a drink with some vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit up is to stay awake late rather than going to bed.

clue.text: Shallot men tended in here

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is sitting within the run of words

explanation.surface: A plot of land where men grow and tend shallots.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as containing it in Shallot men tended.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a rented garden plot where people grow vegetables such as shallots.

clue.text: Slot for post in access

parts.note: the opening in a front door through which mail is pushed, giving the postman a way in

explanation.surface: A hole in the door that lets mail through.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterbox is the slot in a door or wall into which mail is delivered.

clue.text: Comparatively droll you and I'll get about railway, right

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: you and I together are we

explanation.surface: We'll be drier and funnier about the railway, right?
explanation.definitionFit: Wry means drily humorous, so wryer is drier in humour, comparatively droll.

clue.text: Prophetic book, your gentle breeze

parts.note: Zeph is the abbreviation for Zephaniah, a prophetic book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Your prophetic book is as gentle as a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a soft, mild west wind.

clue.text: Rudely at playing away

indicators.note: playing away means performing out of position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Behaving rudely while having an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing away' is British slang for being unfaithful, so it signals the anagram and also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual unfaithfulness in marriage, which British slang calls playing away.
